title: Kesavananda Bharati Sripadagalvaru v. State of Kerala

content.caseIdentity: Kesavananda Bharati Sripadagalvaru v. State of Kerala, (1973) 4 SCC 225
content.facts: Challenge to land-reform legislation and connected constitutional amendments affecting the amending power and fundamental rights.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether the power to amend the Constitution includes the power to damage or destroy its basic structure
content.holding: Parliament's power to amend the Constitution does not include the power to alter its basic structure.
content.ratioDecidendi: Article 368 does not enable Parliament to abrogate or destroy the basic structure of the Constitution.
content.presentLegalPosition: The basic-structure doctrine remains controlling Indian constitutional law.
content.relevance: Kesavananda Bharati is central to the development of the basic-structure doctrine and to understanding the constitutional limits on Parliament's power under Article 368. It remains a principal reference point for later constitutional-amendment cases.
